query: Should I add any bond exposure at all, or stay close to 100% equity given my horizon?

recommendations.title: Maintain 100% Equity Allocation - No Bond Exposure Needed
recommendations.summary: Given your aggressive risk tolerance, 15-year horizon, stable income, and age 30 profile, maintaining near 100% equity allocation is optimal for wealth maximization.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your profile is ideal for maximum equity exposure: (1) 15-year time horizon provides ample recovery time from market volatility, (2) loss comfort of 9/10 indicates psychological readiness for drawdowns, (3) stable $195K income with low expenses ($5.5K/month) provides income cushion, (4) existing emergency fund eliminates need for portfolio liquidity, (5) age 30 means decades of compounding ahead. Bonds would only reduce expected returns (~6-7% vs 10%+ for equities) without meaningful benefit at your life stage. Historical data shows 100% equity outperforms balanced portfolios over 15+ year periods. Your FIRE goal of $2.5M requires maximizing growth - bonds would be a drag on performance.
recommendations.suggested_action: Continue current equity-focused strategy with 0% bond allocation

recommendations.title: Reduce Technology Concentration Risk
recommendations.summary: Your 65% technology sector allocation creates significant concentration risk. Diversify into other growth sectors while maintaining aggressive equity positioning.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: While tech has performed well, 65% concentration in a single sector exposes you to sector-specific risks (regulatory changes, rate sensitivity, cyclical downturns). Your top holdings (QQQ, NVDA, GOOGL, META, AMZN, TSLA) have significant overlap and correlation. Recommend reducing tech to 40-45% and adding exposure to: Healthcare/Biotech (10-15% via XLV, IBB), Industrials (5-10% via XLI), Financials (5-10% via XLF), and International Growth (10-15% via VXUS, VWO). This maintains aggressive growth posture while reducing single-sector dependency. VTI provides some diversification but your individual stock picks heavily tilt portfolio back to tech. Better diversification improves risk-adjusted returns without sacrificing growth potential.
recommendations.suggested_action: Trim tech exposure from 65% to 40-45%, add healthcare, industrials, financials, and international

recommendations.title: Reduce Crypto Allocation from 5% to 2-3%
recommendations.summary: While crypto fits your aggressive profile, 5% allocation may be excessive given extreme volatility. Rebalance to 2-3% for asymmetric upside with controlled risk.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Bitcoin's volatility (60-80% annual) significantly exceeds even aggressive equity portfolios (15-25%). At 5% allocation ($9,000), a 50% crypto drawdown creates $4,500 loss - manageable but inefficient. Studies suggest optimal crypto allocation for aggressive portfolios is 2-5%, with 2-3% providing similar upside capture while reducing portfolio volatility. Your core wealth-building should occur through proven equity markets. Recommend trimming BTC position from 5% to 2-3%, redeploying proceeds to diversified equity positions (international or underrepresented sectors). This maintains speculative exposure for potential asymmetric returns while reducing overall portfolio standard deviation. If crypto thesis remains strong, 2-3% can still generate meaningful wealth if BTC appreciates 5-10x over your horizon.
recommendations.suggested_action: Reduce BTC from 5% to 2-3%, redeploy to international equities

recommendations.title: Deploy Excess Cash - Reduce from 10% to 3-5%
recommendations.summary: Your 10% cash allocation ($18,000) is excessive given low liquidity needs and existing emergency fund. Deploy 5-7% into equities immediately.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: With emergency fund already established, stable income, and low liquidity needs, holding 10% cash creates drag on returns. Cash earns ~4-5% in high-yield savings versus 10%+ equity expected returns - opportunity cost of $900-1,080 annually on $18,000. Recommend maintaining only 3-5% cash ($5,400-9,000) for opportunistic buying during dips and tactical flexibility. Deploy remaining $9,000-12,600 into: (1) International diversification via VXUS/VWO (40%), (2) Underrepresented sectors like healthcare XLV (40%), (3) Adding to VTI for broad market exposure (20%). Given your 15-year horizon and aggressive profile, time in market beats timing the market. Dollar-cost average deployment over 2-3 months if concerned about entry timing, but get capital working sooner.
recommendations.suggested_action: Deploy $9,000-12,600 from cash to diversified equity positions
